text: for the meshing, im wondering if we can either try and make a tool to smooth out my own changes to something since claude clearly can round the mesh properly but cant shape it. i shaped it but its very low poly effect which i think if we get the matrix data we can use it to edit by hand and get a few samples?
resolution: Built both halves of the ask (MESHSMOOTH-0606, commit 8c467a57a). The SMOOTH tool: a 'smooth' brush joined raise/carve/flatten — paint it on the unwrap canvas or grab-drag it directly on the 3D mesh (drag distance is the smoothing dose at the grabbed cell), plus a one-press 'smooth part' action with strength and smooth-passes knobs; it is neighborhood relaxation over the same 48×24 deformation grid every sculpt tool edits, seam-aware, undoable with ctrl+z, and it provably never grows the silhouette past what was shaped — your pulled shape keeps its reach while its surface rounds. THE MATRIX DATA: 'save sample' exports the selected part's grid as a readable JSON file (one row of 48 numbers per line, hand-editable) to cart/hmsc-int/sessions/sculpt-grids/, each saved sample appears as a chip that reapplies it exactly — so you can pull a few samples of shapes you like, hand-edit or hand off a grid file for numeric rounding, and load it back. Honest finding, measured from your actual shaped torso: the low-poly effect is roughness (neighboring grid cells jumping 0.154 on average where smooth parts sit at 0.007), not grid resolution — smoothing attacks exactly that number, and the status line shows it drop when you press smooth part. Resolution remains a smaller secondary ceiling, documented with the upgrade knob in the CAPTURE rather than papered over. 9/9 new behavior tests; both /characters and the workbench stage carry the identical tools.
